From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@olivehealth.com>, Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Engine recommendations and prioritized decision pack — Olive Health POC

Hi Alex / Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — appreciated the clarity on your ingestion cadence and the 95th percentile latency target for clinical summarization (<= 300ms). Per our call I pulled together a concise recommendation pack: prioritized engine slate, expected latency/cost buckets, a short prompt set to validate quality, and the follow-up asks to get a staging pilot running. See attachments: olive_benchmarks_q4.csv, prompt_set_v1.txt, cost_latency_model.xlsx.

High-level recommendation (prioritized):
1) Redwood-Opt-8Q (FP16) — Best quality at target latency on our Dedicated baseline; good for long-context summarization where fidelity matters.
2) Redwood-Lite-4 (int8) — Lowest per-token cost; acceptable on short summarization passes and user-facing previews.
3) Redwood-Fallback-2 (quantized) — Reserve as a fall-back for burst capacity and lower-priority batch jobs.

Rationale (short):
- Quality: Opt-8Q > Lite-4 > Fallback-2 on our clinical prompt-set (see prompt_set_v1).
- Latency: Opt-8Q meets 95th percentile when pinned on Dedicated with batching disabled for low tail latency; Lite-4 has a 25–40% lower cost but ~1.8x higher 95th p in our small-scale tests.
- Cost: Lite-4 reduces per-token spend substantially; we show a hybrid pattern (Opt for final outputs, Lite for previews) that meets your cost constraint of ~$0.02/interaction (estimated).

Next operational asks to start a 2-week staging pilot:
- Confirm which dataset subset we should preload into prefix cache (HIPAA-safe depersonalized set) — ~10k records.
- Week-of-start SLA window (preferred week of Nov 9 or Nov 16).
- PO or test-rate-card approval so we can allocate Dedicated capacity (POC deal id OLV-2026-092).

I called out a few quality risks in the attached notes (row tags in olive_benchmarks_q4.csv) — the main one is hallucination rates on complex multi-hop clinical notes; we recommend a prompt-guardrail and a regression test set.

I'll check in with Ben and Marissa on ops and rollout cadence; Alex / Sofia let me know if you want a short follow-up workshop to walk the prompt pack.

Thanks,
Naomi

Subject: Re: Engine recommendations and prioritized decision pack — Olive Health POC

Naomi — nice concise pack. A few operational notes from infra/cost side: 

- Dedicated sizing: to hit ~300ms 95th p with Opt-8Q we recommend a 2-GPU slice (A40/NVIDIA equivalent) with pinning; that supports ~12 rps sustained. For your expected peak (25 rps), we suggest autoscale with a warm standby Lite-4 pool.
- Hybrid pattern: route finalization calls (after human review) to Opt-8Q; use Lite-4 for real-time previews. We can automate routing in the policy layer.
- Cost sensitivity: cost_latency_model.xlsx has toggles — if Olive wants to constrain monthly to $12k, we need to keep previews on Lite-4 for >=60% of requests.

Operational risk: the benchmark shows a mode collapse on one prompt variant (row tag: "multi-hop-clinical-3"). Recommend adding a focused regression which includes 300 examples from your corpus flagged in the CSV (we'll keep them de-identified).

I'll prepare a short runbook for the staging pilot and a checklist for data ingest privacy (KMS/HSM, audit log hooks). Marissa — can you lead the runbook? Karthik — can you confirm quantization profile we should use for Lite-4 (int8 asymmetric or dynamic)?

-Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Alex — quick answers inline + next steps: 

1) Regression runs: Redwood can host and run the regression on our infra with a short-term scoped access model — we will not store raw PHI in our systems. We will ask Olive to provide de-identified examples and sign the Data Handling Addendum (link in the drive). We'll run the suite and share results via the Drive link; if you prefer we can also provide a signed execution report.

2) Fallback logic: primary behavior is graceful fallback to Lite-4 with an explicit "summary-quality" header returned to the API. If Opt-8Q is unavailable we will:
   - Route to Lite-4 and mark as "preview-quality" (user-visible badge).
   - If Lite-4 is also saturated, we will queue requests briefly (max 2s) then return a cached summary if available; we avoid partial/incoherent responses by preferring cached or preview-quality outputs rather than truncating.

Procurement: loop in Marissa (cc'd) — she handles PO and test-rate-card approvals. Marissa, can you confirm the POC discount band and send a short procurement checklist to Alex?

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- Nov 2: sign DDA and agree dataset subset for regression (Alex / Sofia)
- Nov 9: 2-week staging pilot start (allocate Dedicated slice)
- Nov 23: wrap + results review and go/no-go discussion

Alex/Sofia — are you good to proceed with Nov 9 start if the DDA + PO check are green?

Thanks,
Naomi
